problem: Byzantine nodes in decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning for networked service systems can exploit unbounded state spaces to destabilize both learning and queueing processes.
approach: Proposes a resilient consensus-based MARL algorithm where cooperative agents learn control policies via actor-critic with linear function approximation while communicating with neighbors; mitigates adversarial parameter manipulation through robust consensus mechanisms.
contribution: Proves that cooperative agents' policies converge almost surely to a bounded neighborhood of a stationary solution under mild assumptions, and demonstrates the framework's effectiveness on semantic routing, distributed polling, and smart manufacturing logistics.

problem: Cross-tokenizer knowledge distillation fails when vocabulary overlap is low due to severe alignment noise, causing negative transfer compared to supervised fine-tuning.
approach: Introduces Entropy-aware Span-Constrained Optimal Transport (E-SCOT), which treats distillation as a sparse transport problem using vocabulary-agnostic ground metrics and span-anchored lexical alignment to construct a deterministic support set in linear time.
contribution: E-SCOT achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse model families and eliminates negative transfer even in challenging low-overlap scenarios through Rényi-entropy adaptive reweighting.

problem: Existing instance-wise feature selection methods for explaining black-box model predictions suffer from information leakage, lack of differentiability, and slow training.
approach: Presents Hide&Seek, an end-to-end differentiable model that jointly learns feature selection and prediction under a single objective; reformulates feature removal as a differentiable operation by replacing a proportion of each feature rather than discretely removing them.
contribution: Hide&Seek outperforms existing state-of-the-art models across experiments, is fast to train, and achieves stable training via parsimony-weight annealing.

problem: Existing methods for coupling structural and functional connectivity lack principled formulation grounded in neural communication dynamics, limiting quantification of how information is routed between neural regions.
approach: Formulates multi-modal fusion through neural communication dynamics and proposes Adaptive Flow Routing Network (AFR-Net), a physics-informed framework that models how structural constraints give rise to functional communication patterns.
contribution: AFR-Net significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in discovering critical neural pathways and explaining SC-FC coupling and heterogeneity.

problem: Generalizing motion representation across diverse characters is challenging due to significant topological variations in skeletal structures that hinder development of scalable generative models.
approach: Proposes a Semantic-Aware Topology-Agnostic framework that learns a unified latent manifold using semantic modulation to align functional joint correspondences, thereby decoupling motion from topology.
contribution: Achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from large-scale unaligned raw BVH data, enables zero-shot cross-species retargeting without paired data, and supports downstream text-to-motion tasks.

problem: Softmax attention in large language models suffers from numerical instability and reduced performance as the number of inference tokens increases, limiting length extrapolation.
approach: Proposes a two-stage attention mechanism: first stage replaces Softmax with Softplus followed by l1-normalisation with dynamic scale based on invariance entropy; second stage introduces a re-weighting mechanism that amplifies significant attentional weights to mitigate attention sink.
contribution: The novel attention maintains nearly constant validation loss at 16× training length, outperforms Softmax and state-of-the-art Softmax-free alternatives on long-context retrieval tasks.

problem: The learnability of test-time adaptation under non-stationary streams lacks a principled theoretical framework that captures both continuously evolving distribution shifts and intrinsic information constraints.
approach: Introduces the first theoretical framework for studying TTA learnability with Recovery Complexity and TTA Learnability metrics; proposes a discrete surrogate for non-stationary test streams enabling unified analysis of gradual and abrupt shifts.
contribution: Derives order-wise matching lower and upper bounds on recovery complexity, revealing fundamental limits of TTA and an intrinsic adaptivity-information trade-off with unified learnability guarantees.

problem: Existing online benchmarks for mobile GUI agents are app-centric and task-homogeneous, failing to reflect diversity and instability of real-world mobile usage and causing performance gaps.
approach: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile with user-intent-driven task design reflecting real mobile usage and capability-oriented annotation scheme for fine-grained agent behavior analysis.
contribution: Reveals large performance gaps relative to prior benchmarks, shows failures dominated by perception and memory deficiencies, and demonstrates agents exhibit near-zero success under environment variations.

problem: Distributed bilevel optimization over time-varying directed networks remains largely unexplored due to compounded challenges of consensus bias in dynamic unbalanced communication and nested optimization structure.
approach: Proposes FAB, a fully first-order distributed gradient-based algorithm integrating Push-Pull communication strategy with value function-based penalty method for distributed bilevel optimization.
contribution: Establishes non-asymptotic convergence properties and resolves an open question about Push-Pull algorithm convergence over time-varying directed graphs; validates effectiveness on hyperparameter tuning, data hyper-cleaning, and RL.

problem: Medical MLLMs struggle with complex clinical tasks requiring dynamic and iterative focusing on fine-grained visual regions rather than just generating step-by-step textual reasoning.
approach: Introduces Ophiuchus, a tool-augmented framework where an MLLM decides when to probe fine-grained visual regions, determines where within the image to probe, and weaves sub-image content into an interleaved multimodal chain of thought.
contribution: Outperforms both closed-source and open-source methods across diverse medical benchmarks including VQA, detection, and reasoning-based segmentation through three-stage training: cold-start SFT, self-reflection fine-tuning, and agentic tool reinforcement learning.

problem: Architectures like CNNs, Transformers, and SSMs are hindered by static or time-domain-exclusive designs, limiting their representational flexibility for DNA modeling with complex local motifs, long-range dependencies, and periodic signals.
approach: Introduces Synergistic Plasticity Unit (SPU) with three synergistic layers: Locus Plasticity Layer for fine-grained local motifs via token-specific convolution, Domain Plasticity Layer for multi-domain global features via sequential and spectral patterns, and Saliency Plasticity Layer for optimized information flow.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on DNA modeling with quasi-linear complexity and provides theoretical analysis supporting the unified design paradigm.

problem: Trajectory inference from snapshot data is non-identifiable from finitely many marginals, leaving held-out marginal prediction as the dominant evaluation protocol, which provides limited assessment of inferred dynamics.
approach: Introduces a general framework for estimating Kullback-Leibler divergence between probability measures on function space through a tractable, data-driven estimator scalable to realistic snapshot datasets.
contribution: Validates functional KL enables coherent comparison of trajectory inference methods and exposes discrepancies in inferred dynamics, especially in sparse or missing data regions; demonstrates path-space KL as a principled criterion for evaluation under partial observability.

problem: Dynamical system identification from a single trajectory becomes intractable when the system exhibits unknown symmetries or equivariances imposed by physical laws.
approach: Studies adaptive symmetry discovery for systems with unknown group symmetries; proposes a method to learn the symmetry group directly from a single trajectory and incorporate it into identification, achieving optimal trajectory length.
contribution: Shows systems with known symmetries can be identified from significantly shorter trajectories than generic settings; provides group representation theory and Cayley graph analysis for symmetry discovery.

problem: Bundle-valued statistics on manifolds require transporting observations to common reference fibers, introducing curvature and holonomy effects absent from classical concentration theory.
approach: Develops non-asymptotic concentration theory for transported empirical means on manifolds, deriving Hoeffding and Bernstein-type bounds via sharp Hilbert-space inequalities; isolates holonomy bias through bundle curvature.
contribution: Establishes minimax optimal rates with dimension-free bounds, separating stochastic fluctuation from curvature-driven error floor; provides robust median-of-means estimator and central limit theorem in reference fiber.

problem: Vision-Language Models predominantly digest high-bitrate compressed images; their ability to interpret low-bitrate compressed images remains largely unexplored.
approach: Introduces the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating VLM performance on compressed images across codecs and tasks with over one million images; categorizes performance gaps into information loss and generalization failure.
contribution: Proposes a universal VLM adaptor that improves performance across varying codecs and bitrates by 10%-30% through identifying that only generalization gap can be mitigated for compressed images.

problem: Recurrent networks struggle to effectively encode information about past inputs in evolving dynamics rather than converging to static attractors, hindered by vanishing and exploding gradients.
approach: Develops a theoretical framework using dynamic mean-field theory and diffusion physics; derives a Fisher information diffusion operator linking network connectivity to time-resolved information propagation; proposes principled initialization balancing stability and sensitivity.
contribution: Reveals that operating near criticality is necessary but insufficient for reliable memory; effective retention requires alignment between input-output structure and stable dynamical subspaces; demonstrates faster convergence and higher accuracy on copy task and sequential MNIST.

problem: Diffusion models excel at generative tasks for continuous and token-based domains but their application to discrete ordinal data remains underdeveloped.
approach: Presents CountsDiff, a diffusion framework designed to model distributions on natural numbers; extends Blackout diffusion with survival probability parameterization and incorporates continuous-time training, classifier-free guidance, and churn reverse dynamics.
contribution: Matches or surpasses state-of-the-art discrete generative models and scRNA-seq imputation methods on single-cell RNA data while leaving substantial headroom for optimization.

problem: Compositional planning with temporally extended actions struggles with compounding errors in long-horizon predictions that make estimating visitation distribution induced by sequencing policies intractable.
approach: Learns jumpy world models capturing state occupancies induced by pre-trained policies across multiple timescales; enhances with consistency objective aligning predictions across timescales; combines generative predictions to estimate value of arbitrary policy sequences.
contribution: Compositional planning significantly improves zero-shot performance on challenging manipulation and navigation tasks, yielding 200% relative improvement on average over planning with primitive actions.

problem: Vision-Language Models like CLIP degrade significantly in cross-domain scenarios with scarce target-domain data due to uniform alignment paradigms causing excessive overfitting.
approach: Proposes Adaptive Tail-Head Alignment (ATHA) that adaptively strengthens alignment for tokens with sufficient semantic information and weakens alignment for low-similarity tail tokens, transforming uniform to adaptive alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on four challenging CDFSL benchmarks by exploiting the counterintuitive finding that pushing away tail tokens from textual embeddings improves target-domain performance.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models for robot manipulation have representations lacking sensitivity to robotic signals such as control actions and proprioceptive information.
approach: Introduces Robot State-aware Contrastive Loss (RS-CL) that aligns representations with robot proprioceptive states by using relative distances between states as soft supervision, complementing action prediction objectives.
contribution: RS-CL substantially improves performance of state-of-the-art VLA models, achieving 69.7% on RoboCasa-Kitchen benchmark and boosting success rates from 45.0% to 58.3% on challenging real-robot manipulation tasks.

problem: Post-training quantization for W4A4 LLMs remains open, and existing methods designed for INT4 formats suffer from incompatibility with emerging MXFP4 format due to its power-of-two block scaling.
approach: Analyzes the fundamental mismatch between MXFP4's power-of-two block scaling and global rotation-based optimization; proposes a simple block rotation strategy adapting rotation-based methods to MXFP4.
contribution: Provides first in-depth analysis of rotation-based quantization incompatibility with MXFP4 and achieves substantial accuracy improvements across diverse LLMs through block rotation adaptation.

problem: Fine-tuned models on small, imbalanced medical datasets often become overconfident due to norm bias, where predictions rely on feature magnitude rather than semantic alignment.
approach: Proposes Spherical Procrustes Alignment (SPA) combining spherical constraints with dynamic Equiangular Tight Frame alignment; uses Spherical branch to eliminate norm bias via normalization and Geometric branch to adapt features via Procrustes alignment.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on medical audio diagnosis datasets (ICBHI 2017, CirCor DigiScope) and transforms pre-trained models into reliable clinical tools without extra inference cost.

problem: Text-to-video generation methods output only final composited video and lack editable layered representations, limiting use in professional workflows.
approach: Proposes LayerT2V, which produces multiple semantically consistent outputs in a single pass: full video, background layer, and multiple foreground RGB layers with alpha mattes; serializes layer representations along temporal dimension using high compression.
contribution: Substantially outperforms prior methods in visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and cross-layer coherence; introduces VidLayer, the first large-scale dataset for multi-layer video generation.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts LLM compression via SVD overlooks heterogeneous expert utilization where routing frequency and information density vary significantly across experts.
approach: Proposes RFID-MoE combining expert activation frequency with effective rank to measure importance, adaptively allocating ranks; reconstructs compression residuals via sparse projection mechanism.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving perplexity of 16.92 on PTB with Qwen3-30B at 60% compression ratio, reducing perplexity by over 8.0 compared to baselines.

problem: Practical deployment of LLM-based automated assessment faces persistent challenges: heterogeneous reliability across models, substantial latency and token costs, and lack of principled strategies for resource allocation.
approach: Introduces R²Eval, a routing-aware framework formulating evaluation as resource allocation and aggregation; combines difficulty-aware routing with reasoned evaluation signals to dynamically select evaluator models under accuracy, latency, and cost constraints.
contribution: Provides systematic analysis of how reasoning traces correlate with assessment outcomes; develops offline and online routing strategies achieving substantially improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across 19 language models.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle with complex manipulation tasks requiring high dexterity and generalization due to reliance on synthetic data with significant sim-to-real gaps or limited demonstrations.
approach: Leverages human hands as manipulator template and large-scale human video for VLA pretraining; introduces physical instruction tuning combining VLA pretraining, perspective spatial alignment, and post-training adaptation; develops part-level motion tokenization for millimeter-level accuracy.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance in hand motion generation, favorable scaling laws, and promising capabilities in robotic dexterous manipulation, validating effectiveness of bridging human-robot embodiment gap.

problem: Building LLM workflows typically relies on human-crafted pipelines and prompts, presenting a substantial bottleneck in real-world deployment of AI systems.
approach: Proposes FlowBot, a data-driven approach formulating workflow induction as bilevel optimization: outer loop optimizes workflow sketch structure, inner loop optimizes individual LLM calls via backpropagating textual gradients layer-by-layer.
contribution: Discovered workflows perform competitively against strong baselines using human-crafted or generated workflows.

problem: Post-training quantization of LLMs struggles with temporal inconsistency, invalidation of Round-to-Nearest assumptions, and spatially-inconsistent optimization objectives when synergizing learning-based and compensation-based rounding.
approach: Introduces STLA with cluster-wise integrated rounding optimization resolving temporal inconsistency; achieves spatial alignment through unified global objective derived from Schur Complement; employs Hessian-guided clustering.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art for low-bit PTQ while maintaining computational efficiency.

problem: Continual learning on pretrained models faces practical barriers where pretraining distributions are unavailable and requires access to old-task data.
approach: Develops PLATE exploiting geometric redundancy in pretrained networks; constructs protected update subspaces from pretrained weights; parameterizes each layer with structured low-rank update where frozen components from pretrained weights and trainable component adapts to new task.
contribution: Provides explicit control over plasticity-retention trade-off without past-task data access and maintains worst-case retention guarantees.

problem: Large language models cannot reliably recognize their parametric knowledge boundaries and often hallucinate answers to out-of-boundary questions.
approach: Introduces MASH (Modeling Abstention via Selective Help-seeking) using reinforcement learning with pay-per-search reward, where external search tool use serves as proxy for abstention when penalized.
contribution: Substantially improves selective help-seeking performance on multi-hop datasets by 7.6%, demonstrates strong off-the-shelf abstention performance competitive with prior methods.

problem: Current AI-Generated Image detectors learn entangled forgery representations, conflating content-dependent flaws with content-agnostic artifacts, and are limited by outdated benchmarks.
approach: Proposes OmniAID with decoupled Mixture-of-Experts architecture: Routable Specialized Semantic Experts separate semantic flaws across domains, Fixed Universal Artifact Expert isolates content-agnostic universal artifacts; employs two-stage training with hard-sampling and lightweight gating.
contribution: Surpasses existing detectors with robust generalization across diverse generative models; introduces Mirage dataset with modern training and challenging test sets.

problem: Comparative capabilities of chain of thought versus latent thought reasoning in large language models remain underexplored despite both exploiting iterative computation.
approach: Presents formal analysis showing latent thought admits efficient parallel computation while CoT is inherently sequential; conversely, CoT enables approximate counting via stochastic decoding.
contribution: Provides formal separations suggesting tasks where depth-driven recursion is more suitable, offering practical guidance for choosing between reasoning paradigms.

problem: Flow-based generative models lack diagnostic tools to assess how much effort trajectories require and how this relates to generation quality and memorization.
approach: Introduces Kinetic Path Energy (KPE), an action-like per-sample diagnostic measuring accumulated kinetic effort along ODE trajectory; develops Kinetic Trajectory Shaping (KTS), a training-free two-phase inference strategy.
contribution: Shows KPE exhibits robust correspondences with semantic fidelity and sparse representation regions; demonstrates non-monotonic correlation at high energy (memorization degeneration); KTS reduces memorization and improves generation quality.

problem: Parallel thinking for reasoning imposes significant computational burdens; existing efficiency methods rely on local per-trajectory signals and lack global mechanisms to exploit dynamics across parallel branches.
approach: Introduces 2D probing exposing width-depth dynamics by eliciting intermediate answers from all branches periodically; develops Parallel-Probe controller with consensus-based early stopping and deviation-based branch pruning.
contribution: Establishes superior Pareto frontier for test-time scaling, reducing sequential tokens by up to 35.8% and total token cost by over 25.8% compared to majority voting.

problem: Code transformation tasks rely on implicit representation construction in model weights or rigid compiler-level abstractions rather than constructing high-quality representations explicitly.
approach: Presents SemRep employing semantics-preserving transformations as intermediate representation; serves both as generative mid-training task and guidance for instruction-specific transformations.
contribution: Outperforms extensively finetuned baselines by 6.9% in correctness, 1.1× in performance, 13.9% in generalization, and 6.7% in robustness; with evolutionary agent finds optimizations that 685B larger-weight baselines miss.

problem: GPU kernel optimization by LLM agents remains inefficient due to fundamental mismatch between LLM generation capabilities and vast optimization search space over diverse hardware.
approach: Formulates kernel optimization as Multi-Armed Bandit problem; designs hardware-aware pruning via profiling bounds and runtime-behavior clustering leveraging Lipschitz continuity to navigate infinite arm space.
contribution: Consistently outperforms strongest agent baseline, achieving up to 1.91× geometric mean speedup with 39-140% relative improvement in Fast@1 success rate across three GPU architectures.

problem: Natural language instructions are often underspecified, mapping to multiple valid yet functionally distinct latent intents; LLMs remain limited in interactive disambiguation due to semantic blindness.
approach: Proposes Topological Active Inference (TAI) recasting task disambiguation as intent-manifold contraction; uses Persistent Homology to recover persistent intent clusters; selects clarifying questions with Topological Expected Information Gain.
contribution: Reduces effective hypothesis space from N sampled solutions to K latent intents with logarithmic interaction complexity O(log K); resolves user intent with fewer turns and robustness to noisy feedback.

problem: Text-to-image generation models lack fine-grained control over generated images due to limited understanding of how semantic information is encoded in latent space.
approach: Develops interpretation of color representation in Variational Autoencoder latent space revealing structure reflecting Hue, Saturation, and Lightness; leverages closed-form latent-space manipulation.
contribution: Introduces fully training-free method in FLUX for predicting and explicitly controlling color through Latent Color Subspace interpretation.

problem: Flow map matching for one- and few-step sampling suffers from mismatch between ground-truth training transitions and model-induced flow maps, hindering performance.
approach: Proposes Contrastive Flow Map Matching (CFMM) motivated by joint-KL decomposition on reverse KL; combines average-velocity regression for marginal alignment with sampling-aligned InfoNCE contrastive loss.
contribution: Achieves consistent improvements in fidelity and perceptual quality across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and LSUN with only modest additional training cost and no inference-time overhead.

problem: Decentralized online convex optimization with compressed communication suffers from prohibitively high quadratic or quartic dependence on compression quality factor and super-linear dependence on number of learners.
approach: Proposes novel algorithm with two-level blocking update framework incorporating online gossip strategy and error compensation scheme; establishes improved regret bounds and first lower bounds for the problem.
contribution: Achieves improved regret bounds of Õ(ω^{-1/2}ρ^{-1}n√T) and Õ(ω^{-1}ρ^{-2}n ln T) for convex and strongly convex functions, justifying optimality with respect to compression quality and time horizon.
